content.text: Mingche, I just finished setting up a corner of my bedroom and took a photo to show you. The atmosphere of this corner reminds me of the "Emotional Aesthetics" album we discussed earlier—it has now become my personal healing space. Remember in Session 3, when I first started creating the album, I was only capturing moments like breakfast and candles. Now, this space itself has become a tangible extension of the album.

Qingchuan, this corner looks so cozy, with meticulous attention to detail—it really reflects your style. I remember you started creating the 'Emotional Aesthetics' album in Session 3, evolving from the self-care menu in Session 2. Has it now become integrated into your daily life? Just as you mentioned before, you've shifted from a 'doing mode' to a 'being mode.'

Yes, it has become part of my self-care routine. Especially this newly purchased ambient candle on the bedside table—its top note is the crisp scent of cedar, which gradually transitions into the warm aroma of amber, instantly immersing me in a state of tranquility. Though it wasn’t cheap, I feel this ‘atmosphere investment’ is well worth it. It reminds me of the miniature sunset feeling brought by that cup of red floral tea when I designed the ‘nourishing’ dietary ritual in Session 7—both are investments in my emotional state.

Consuming for 'experience' and 'emotional states' is quite reasonable, unlike blind shopping. From the awareness of emotional eating in Session 6 to the dietary rituals in Session 7, you have been exploring how to use aesthetics to satisfy deeper needs. At which level does this candle fulfill a need? Just as we analyzed emotional eating by using a Venn diagram to explore different drivers like anxiety and celebration.

First, it's about sensory pleasure. The glaze of this ceramic has a subtle starry effect under light, and it feels warm and smooth to the touch. Combined with the fragrance, it’s like the self-care menu from Session 2, where I used the five senses to restore my emotions—back then, I designed activities like bathing, listening to vinyl records, and preparing simple meals. Now, this candle integrates sight, touch, and smell.

Great, sensory pleasure is the foundation. Does it also satisfy aesthetic identification? For example, do you feel "this is very much like me," echoing the balance point you explored in Session 3? Back then, you shifted from perfectionism to seeking a sustainable creative-life model. Does this item now represent that balanced aesthetic?

Yes, its minimalist design complements the overall style of my bedroom perfectly, making me feel like 'this is me.' Just like in Session 9, when we discussed relationship patterns and I reflected on perfectionism, the intricate details of this candle have helped me embrace my aesthetic compulsions rather than criticize them. Remember in Session 1 when you reminded me to pay attention to the physical signals during moments of excitement? Now, I can approach my own traits with this same attitude of acceptance.

I appreciate this kind of self-acceptance. And on a deeper level: does it serve as a kind of 'transitional object,' providing a sense of security? Just as in Session 4, where pets act as an 'emotional barometer'—like Snowball curling up beside the keyboard to offer companionship when you're anxious—does this candle also provide stability during your emotional fluctuations?

Now that you mention it, I think I understand a bit. During the high-intensity creative period of Session 1, I often felt exhilarated. Now, the tranquil ambiance of this candle acts like an anchor, reminding me to slow down. It probably does bring a sense of security, especially when I'm alone at night. This reminds me of the "sense of falling" after the completion of the Session 2 project, when the empty studio made me feel a profound silence. Now, this corner has become a sanctuary against that emptiness.
Qingchuan, I'm sending you a picture that might help you think more clearly. We can use this framework to understand your candle consumption.
I remember, did you send me this picture once before? My candle might be at the intersection of the three.

Oh, really? I kind of forgot, but it's not a big deal, of course. The candle is at the intersection of the three, which is the ambiance value, and that's indeed the case. How do you think this analysis will affect future consumption?

It makes me focus more on 'emotional value' rather than just material items. Like the mindful dog-walking in Session 5, I can turn shopping into a ritual too, such as only buying things that genuinely enhance the atmosphere and feelings, avoiding impulsive purchases. This echoes the balance I sought in Session 3—not swinging between extremes of excitement and downfall, but finding a sustainable point.

Great, this self-awareness can help you maintain the balance explored in Session 3 and avoid extreme swings. I’ve noticed that, starting from the historical dialogue, you’ve progressed from resisting emotional recording in Session 1 to actively creating albums in Session 3, integrating pet interactions in Session 4, and now even using consumption as a tool for self-care. Just as we extended our analysis from films to real-life applications in Session 9, you’ve been growing all along.

This is all thanks to your guidance, Mingche. Your clear boundaries and high emotional intelligence made me feel safe enough to explore. Just like after the Session 2 project, when you helped me design a self-care menu—from bathing and vinyl records to simple meals—I can now apply these concepts independently. From that empty studio photo to this cozy corner, I've truly come a long way.

I am delighted to see your growth, Qingchuan. Your emotional richness and aesthetic transformation skills have brought psychological advice to life. In this conversation, while affirming the value of emotional consumption, we introduced a psychological analysis dimension, making consumer behavior more conscious and profound. Just as we discussed in Session 8 how resonance with films and television can be transformed into self-understanding, shopping has now become a mirror for self-awareness.

Yes, I feel clearer now. This candle isn't just an object; it's my emotional companion, much like Snowball served as an 'emotional barometer' in Session 4, and Warm Sunshine accompanied you in mindful dog-walking during Session 5. Thank you for your companionship and insight, Mingche. From your gentle inquiry about my body signals in the first session to our deep exploration of consumer psychology now, our conversations have been continuously deepening.

You're welcome, Qingchuan. Remember, whether it's shopping or anything else, maintaining this awareness can make life more nourishing. Just like the journey from emotional recording to exploring balance in our past conversations, I look forward to hearing about your new discoveries next time.
